Q: AWS Lambda - python webscraping - unable to bypass cloudfare anti-bots from AWS ip but working from local ip A:

This is a well-known issue — AWS, GCP, and Azure IP ranges are heavily flagged by Cloudflare because they're almost exclusively datacenter/cloud traffic. Cloudflare's challenge triggers much more aggressively on cloud IPs than on residential ones.

A few approaches depending on your constraints:

1. Route Lambda egress through residential IPs: Set up an HTTP proxy (squid, etc.) on a residential or ISP IP, point Lambda requests through it. Adds latency but resolves the IP class problem.

2. Use a Scraping API or residential proxy service with Lambda: Most scraping APIs handle Cloudflare bypass internally. Pass your requests through the API endpoint rather than making direct requests from Lambda.

3. NAT Gateway + Elastic IP: Doesn't help — Elastic IPs are still AWS ranges and will be flagged the same way.

The underlying issue is that Cloudflare knows your request is coming from AWS regardless of headers or UA. Changing the IP class is the only reliable fix.
